body:
### The problem

The expression of a template interpolation is kept as one token for the
states (and in TSX the whole template is one token), so that its braces,
backticks and nested templates cannot move the end of the function. That
design is kept here. But the condition counter sees only that one token, so
the conditions written in an interpolation are not counted:

```js
function label(x, y) {
  return `v: ${x ? 1 : 2} ${x && y}`;
}
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       3      1     19      2       3 label@1-3@a.js
```

The cyclomatic complexity of `label` is 1 instead of 3 in .js, .ts, .jsx and
.tsx, while the same expressions outside the template give 3.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_templates.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript.py`. The TypeScript reader, which the four
extensions use, now tokenizes the code of each interpolation, at any depth of
nesting, and counts its conditions; the tokens given to the states do not
change. The code is found with the same scan that splits the templates,
extended so that nested templates split the code around them and every
character is read once: a template nested 5000 times deep is still read in
linear time. Text, strings, comments and regex literals inside the template
are not counted. With the fix:

```
       3      3     19      2       3 label@1-3@a.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_conditions_in_template_interpolations` in
`test/test_languages/testTypeScript.py`, with subtests for the four
extensions, which fail on `master` without the change. The full suite passes
on the branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1666 passed, 7 skipped.
pycodestyle reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

The tokens the states receive, so the start and end of functions, and the
token count.

If #546 is merged too, a keyword used as a member
name inside an interpolation, `${p.catch(f)}`, is still counted as a
condition, because the code of the interpolation is tokenized apart. I can
send a follow-up for that once both are in.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.
title: Count the conditions in JavaScript/TypeScript template interpolations
